purpose: Controls deliberately left without a HIPAA citation. Each was reviewed on 2026-10-06: its previous citation did not describe what the evaluator checks, and no Security Rule standard or implementation specification is a close enough match to cite instead. An empty citation is more accurate than a stretched one. TP.FrameworkCoverage.Tests.ps1 accepts an empty HIPAA citation only for a control listed here, and fails if a listed control gains one (remove it from this list when a reviewed citation is added).

controls.PVW-2.3: Checks the Information Barriers mode. Its previous citation, 164.308(a)(4)(ii)(A), applies only to a health care clearinghouse within a larger organization, which the tool cannot establish; no other specification describes segmenting communication between internal groups.
controls.DEF-4.4: Checks that accounts are tagged as priority accounts in Defender for Office 365. Tagging is a prerequisite for differentiated protection and alerting, not itself a safeguard the Security Rule names; its previous citation, security reminders (164.308(a)(5)(ii)(A)), is workforce training.
controls.EXO-5.2: Checks that tagged priority accounts are protected by targeted user impersonation protection in the anti-phishing policy. Impersonation protection is not protection from malicious software (164.308(a)(5)(ii)(B)), and its previous citation, security reminders, is workforce training.
controls.TMS-1.5: Checks that Teams meeting recordings are stored in SharePoint/OneDrive under the organization's retention. Its remaining citation, 164.310(d)(2)(ii) media re-use, covers removing ePHI from electronic media before the media is reused, which the check does not examine (found by review of PR #121, 2026-10-07); no other specification describes where recordings are stored.
controls.PPL-4.4: Checks that Copilot Studio email tools do not let the AI set the recipient, subject or body. The Security Rule names no standard for restricting the destinations an application may send data to; transmission security (164.312(e)(1)) concerns protecting data in transit, not where it is sent.
controls.PPL-4.5: Checks that connector tools use end-user rather than maker credentials. That is least privilege for an application acting on a user's behalf; the Security Rule's access control standard (164.312(a)(1)) is about granting access to persons or programs with rights, and no specification describes delegated versus stored connector credentials.
controls.PPL-4.6: A heuristic search for credentials written into agent definitions. No Security Rule specification describes secrets embedded in configuration; person or entity authentication (164.312(d)) is about verifying identity at access, not about where credentials are stored.
controls.PPL-4.7: Lists MCP tool integrations for manual review. Reviewing third-party integrations maps to business associate arrangements only when the provider handles ePHI, which the tool cannot establish.
controls.PPL-4.8: Checks that generative agents carry custom instructions. No Security Rule specification describes constraining an AI agent's behavior.
controls.PPL-4.9: Checks that each agent has an enabled owner. Workforce clearance and termination procedures (164.308(a)(3)) concern a person's access, not the accountability for an application component the person created.
controls.PPL-4.10: Checks agents left unmodified beyond an approved period. No Security Rule specification sets a review interval for application components; the evaluation standard (164.308(a)(8)) is an organization-wide periodic evaluation, not a per-component check.
